Unfortunately there was a failure upon the first charging of that new set (which could've been my fault, even though I had the plug turned in the correct orientation).  I contacted the company via the phone # in the user manual, anticipating the usual corporate run-around. query: I'm looking for earbuds with the best sound quality and without any Bluetooth issues. The sound quality needs to be superb, better than Bose, Momentum, and Sony headphones, and exactly what you'd expect from B&W. I also need them to have a built-in transmitter so I can watch movies on airplane AV systems with no audio lag. However, I wish the cable was attached to the case instead of being loose. It's important for the earbuds to support multiple CODECs, including APT/X. I prefer ear tips that fit well and stay in place, like the ones that came with them. Additionally, I want the Bluetooth dropouts issue to be fixed since it was present in the older model. On the downside, the battery life should be better as it currently only lasts around 4 hours. I've even considered buying a second pair to use while the other is charging because the sound quality is worth it. The active noise cancellation should be decent but not as good as Bose's or Sony's. Lastly, I don't have a preference for the tap system as I can't remember any of them anyway.
review: Best sound quality of any buds. (And they've fixed the bluetooth issues.) Pros: The sound quality is superb, noticeably better than the bose/momentum/sonys and exactly what you'd expect from B&W. That's why they get 5 stars. I also love the built in transmitter so that I can watch movies on airplane AV systems (no noticeable audio lag). I wish the cable was built into the case, rather than being a loose cable that I'll almost certainly lose. They support many CODECs, including APT/X (but not LDAC). The tips that came with them fit my ears well—better than the memory-foam ones—and stay in just fine. The older Pi7 (not S2) buds had issues with Bluetooth dropouts that are completely fixed with the S2 version.  Cons: The battery life is pathetic—maybe 4 hours. Won't even last for a full SF-NYC flight, much less an international one. I've considered getting another pair so I can use one set while the other is charging in the case (the sound quality is that good). The ANC is adequate, but nothing near as good as Bose's or Sony's.  You cannot adjust the volume from the buds.  Neutral: Many reviewers don't like the one-two-three-long-short tap system. I don't much care one way or another about any of that—I can't remember any of the various bud's systems in any event.

I use them for long commutes and airplane movie watching (I need a built‑in transmitter to avoid audio lag on plane AV systems) and for everyday calls, so wireless in‑ears with a good mic are essential. I hate Bluetooth dropouts and expect stable multi‑codec support (including aptX); I also prefer ear tips that stay put during use. Battery life is a real pain point for me — the current set only lasts ~4 hours which won’t cover longer flights — but I might tolerate a shorter battery if the sound is that good. I don’t care about tricky tap control schemes, but I do wish the charging cable were attached to the case so I wouldn’t lose it.

I want earbuds that pair reliably without Bluetooth hiccups and that support multiple CODECs including aptX; ANC should be decent but I don’t expect it to beat Bose or Sony. I need an in‑ear fit that stays in place, a usable microphone for calls, and a build that avoids petty annoyances like a loose charging cable. My budget is about $350–450, maybe up to $500 if the sound and features justify it.
opening: Looking for earbuds with top-tier sound for flights and everyday use, and they must be rock‑solid with Bluetooth.
brief: Wants wireless in‑ear earbuds with audiophile-level sound, built-in airplane transmitter, aptX/multi‑codec support, reliable Bluetooth, decent ANC, and better battery life than ~4 hours.
